guitar.evidence: Steve Vai's Ibanez JEM signature series (with the iconic 'monkey grip' and 'Evo' guitar) is one of the most famous signature guitar lines in rock.

tone.target: nasal high-gain lead with wah and long sustain
tone.profile: nasal high-gain lead with wah and long sustain
tone.summary: Gate 1 -> Boost -> Wah (V-Wah) -> Distortion (Chief) -> Amp (UK 800) -> Cab/IR (UK Vintage 4x12) -> EQ (Guitar EQ 2) -> Chorus -> Delay (Digital Delay) -> Reverb (Plate)

blocks.purpose: Clean up high-gain noise and sustain artifacts.
Sustain and articulate the initial attack for lead lines.
blocks.gap: Using Boost to simulate a clean boost pedal effect, enhancing clarity before high gain.

blocks.purpose: Provide the signature vocal/wah sweeps required for lead playing.
Provide controlled high gain and grit without sounding muddy.
blocks.gap: Chief is chosen for its articulate, aggressive tone suitable for Vai's style, avoiding generic fuzz/crunch.

blocks.purpose: Simulate a powerful, articulate British high-gain tone.
blocks.gap: The UK 800 provides the necessary punch and clarity for modern lead tones.

blocks.purpose: Ground the high-gain tone with a classic, articulate British cabinet sound.
Sculpt the frequency response, ensuring extreme brightness and cutting low-end mud.
blocks.gap: Using EQ 2 for precise high-frequency boosts to enhance articulation.

blocks.purpose: Add subtle width and movement to the sustained lead lines.
blocks.gap: Chorus adds necessary dimension without sacrificing high-gain clarity.

blocks.purpose: Create the signature long, shimmering delay tail.
Provide a large, controlled sense of space and sustain.
blocks.gap: Plate reverb is ideal for adding massive, clear ambience to lead tones.

improvements.summary: Upgrade the cabinet IR to better capture Vai's bright, modern high-gain articulation.

proposals.reason: Enhance brightness and punch for Vai's aggressive lead tone.
proposals.expectedGain: Increased clarity and bite in the high end.
